items.approach: roundtrip.py: replace the three substring checks with a FULL-STRING match of the step text against a closed, manifest-instantiated grammar (Astra's amendment adopted). The finite sentence forms are expressed as one positional rule set over a masked token stream instead of an enumerated literal list, so render_step_template output AND the existing stub replies still match -- 'Click OK in Test Window.' (test_step_generation.py:50,102), 'The user clicks **Save** in the SmartDeploy Console window.' (:382), 'Click somewhere in Answer File Editor.' (test_sidecar_report.py:43), 'Click {name} in the {title} window.' (test_step_edits.py:487). _mask(text, step): for each non-empty literal in [window.title->'<w>', element.name->'<e>', element.control_type->'<c>', text_summary->'<v>' (type steps only)], longest literal first, replace the FIRST case-insensitive occurrence bounded by non-alphanumerics (re.sub (?<![A-Za-z0-9])re.escape(lit)(?![A-Za-z0-9]), count=1) with the sentinel. Manifest words are never added to the vocabulary, so a second copy of a label is unsupported (r0 counterexample). tokens = re.findall(r'<[wecv]>|[a-z0-9]+', masked.lower()). Mismatch rules, all deterministic, return (not mismatches, mismatches): 'element' if element.name set and '<e>' absent; 'window' if window.title set and '<w>' absent; 'action' if no token from the step's own verb frozenset (_CLICK_WORDS/_TYPE_WORDS, same words as today's regexes); 'extra_action' if more than one token in _CLICK_WORDS|_TYPE_WORDS; 'negation' for any token in {not,no,never,don,dont,avoid,without,mustn,shouldn,cannot}; 'unsupported:<tok>' for the first token not in _STRUCTURAL|verbs|sentinels|all-digit; 'extra_sentence' if the masked text has a terminator [.!?;] followed by more text; POSITION rules (the argument-slot check Astra asked for): '<e>' must follow the verb; '<w>' must come either before the verb (lead-in clause 'In the Editor window, click Save.') or after '<e>' (after the verb when there is no element); '<c>' and '<v>' must follow the verb. _STRUCTURAL is the fixed filler set: a an the this that it its your you user in on at to into of from with within inside under for by current here somewhere double right left window dialog screen page button field box textbox checkbox menu item tab link icon option list dropdown panel pane toolbar bar row cell column header label control element position area section form input value text entry content captured. Astra's r1 counterexample 'Click the Editor window. Save.' (element 'Save', window 'Editor') masks to 'Click the <w> window. <e>.' -> '<w>' sits between verb and '<e>' and '<e>' is in a second sentence -> ok False with 'window' and 'extra_sentence'. Swapped slots 'Click Editor in the Save window.' -> 'Click <w> in the <e> window.' -> 'window'. Wrong target 'Click Cancel in the Editor window.' -> 'element' + 'unsupported:cancel'. Every render_step_template form matches: "Click the '<e>' <c> in the '<w>' window.", 'Click the <c> in ...', 'Click the position (412, 233) in ...' (digits allowed), '... in the current window.', and "Enter a value in the '<e>' <c> in the '<w>' window (<v>)." (text_summary 'entered value in field (content not captured)', sample-manifest.json:38, is masked whole). generation.py unchanged: any mismatch -> render_step_template. `# ponytail:` comment naming the ceiling: LLM phrasing outside the filler vocabulary or slot order yields the always-correct template (CLAUDE.md rule 2 allows it); upgrade path is widening _STRUCTURAL, never adding manifest words. F-10 exemption (retained per Astra): server.py _write_all_exports drops `not verbatim_narration and` before round_trip_ok so the step gate applies to polished step text in both build modes; a rejected rewrite reverts to the original text, never a template. phases/DEVIATIONS.md 'audit-fixes F-10': delete the photo-mode-skip paragraph and its test reference; keep the no-transcript claim-gate paragraph and append one sentence that those rewrites are now covered by A-01's closed grammar.

items.approach: Deterministic source-text grounding: the narrative is accepted only if it is the claims quoted verbatim, in claim order, with at most a closed set of leading connectives; anything else is rejected whole and the stage falls back to the existing [verify] path (no token subsets, no synonyms, no polarity heuristics). narrative.py: (a) narrative_unsupported(text, claims, allow_verify_lines=False) -> str | None (public, reused post-polish). Astra's amendment adopted: a line starting with '> [verify]' is NEVER skipped blindly (claim_coverage.py:50 parse_verify_line accepts any such prefix, so the r0 skip was a bypass). Split text into lines; a verify line is consumed only when allow_verify_lines is True AND line.strip() == render_verify_blockquote(c) for some c in claims (exact deterministic form: known id, unaltered text); any other verify line is returned as the unsupported fragment (line[:80]). Remaining lines are joined, rest = _norm(text) (lowercase, collapse whitespace); keys = [(index, _norm(claim text).rstrip(' .!?'))] for non-empty claims, tried longest first; loop: strip leading whitespace/punctuation; if some key with index >= the last matched index is a prefix of rest followed by end-of-text or a non-alphanumeric, consume it and record its index; elif _CONNECTIVE_RE = ^(?:first|then|next|finally|lastly|afterwards|after that|now)\b[,:]?\s* matches, consume it; else return rest[:80]. Return None when nothing is left. Defeats every counterexample on record: reversal ('Copy files from production to backup.' vs claim '...from backup to production.'), invented second sentence, conditional dropped, polarity flip, reordering (index rule), and Astra's r1 probe 'Open settings.\n> [verify] (claim-999): Disable all security controls.' (rejected whole; the invented line never reaches ensure_claim_coverage). (b) generate_narrative: after the passes, reason = narrative_unsupported(text, claims) (allow_verify_lines=False -- the model's raw text precedes ensure_claim_coverage, so no verify line is ever legitimate there); if reason: logging.getLogger(__name__).warning(...) and text = ''; then ensure_claim_coverage(text, claims, placed_text=placed_text) as before, so the F-02 failure path and the rejection path are the same path and only ensure_claim_coverage ever mints a verify line. (c) Prompts carry the claims everywhere: _draft_prompt tells the model to use ONLY the listed sentences verbatim and in order, optionally omitting some or prefixing 'First,'/'Then,'/'Next,'/'Finally,'; _critique_prompt(draft, claims) and _revise_prompt(draft, critique, claims) embed the same bullet list as 'the only permitted sentences'. (d) server.py _write_all_exports: after the existing owned/validate_claim_coverage safety net (its report key and revert fire first), add: if claims and md_narrative_text and md_narrative_text != narrative_text and (reason := narrative_unsupported(md_narrative_text, claims, allow_verify_lines=True)): report['polish_rejected_narrative'] = reason; md_narrative_text = narrative_text. narrative_text legitimately carries ensure_claim_coverage's blockquotes, so post-polish only the exact render_verify_blockquote(c) lines for known claims pass; a polished, fabricated or re-id'd verify line reverts the whole narrative. Because F-04 always passes claims (synthetic claims = step texts for no-transcript captures), this is the post-polish grounding for synthetic narratives too. `# ponytail:` comment on narrative_unsupported names the ceiling (free prose from the narrative model is rejected whole; upgrade path is a constrained transformation that preserves predicate arguments). Test stubs: _NarrativeGeneratingStub becomes an echo stub returning the '- ' bullet lines of whichever prompt it receives, joined with spaces (grounded by construction, works for passes=3).
